label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is TRUE POSITIVE. The resolved sink value on the executed path depends on attacker-controlled input. Code flow: Cookie.getValue (line 59) -> URLDecoder.decode (line 61) -> param (line 61) -> conditional assignment to bar (line 76) -> bar assigned to inputParam (line 83) -> input bytes derived from inputParam (line 84) -> new String(input) (line 109) -> encodeForHTML(new String(input)) (line 110). Although ESAPI.encodeForHTML sanitizes XSS characters, the sink expression itself outputs the sanitized user-supplied content directly into the HTTP response body ('Sensitive value '...''). This constitutes a reflected XSS vulnerability where the application echoes user input back to them, potentially allowing script execution if the input bypasses certain filters or if the sanitizer is insufficient against specific payloads. The resolved sink value is the encoded version of the user's cookie value.

evidence.note: User input flows from Cookie.getValue(L59) through decoding and conditional logic to become 'bar' (L76), then 'input' (L84), and finally printed via encodeForHTML in the response writer (L104-L110).
